Preserve Protected-peer’s supplied association. Inspect the current chain and verify every required node; merely configuring one device is incomplete.

lesson.prerequisite_note: You can identify a supplied IPv4 device and distinguish an IP address from a device label. No NTP administrator or terminal experience is assumed. Client/server roles, strata, configuration removal, read-only diagnostics and policy checks are taught below before this task. All work stays in the simulator.

concepts.title: Client and server are roles in a dependency chain
concepts.text: A client asks its configured upstream for time; a synchronized network device may then serve downstream clients. A root reference is supplied evidence here. A stratum is a place in a hierarchy, not a measurement of accuracy: a device derives its upstream stratum plus one. Unsynchronized state is shown as16. This simulator recomputes dependencies immediately and does not move a real clock or prove correct UTC.

concepts.title: Configure one association on the selected device
concepts.text: Choose a supplied device, type ntp server IPv4, then Run. A second different server is deliberately unsupported in this single-upstream model: use no ntp server OLD before ntp server NEW. Show running-config reads the configured association; show ntp status and show ntp associations derive current state. SIM select IPv4 in a walkthrough is only an app navigation helper; use the native Selected device dropdown. It is not an IOS command.

concepts.title: Configured does not mean synchronized
concepts.text: Follow the entire currently configured chain. A device without a source, an unknown address, an offline or unhealthy source, or an exhausted stratum prevents service. A cycle means A asks B while B asks A: neither chain reaches an independent reference, so neither can synchronize. A healthy alternate reference does nothing until you explicitly configure a supported path to it.

concepts.title: Both directions and UDP123 matter
concepts.text: The supplied delivery table separates the client request, server reply and UDP123 permission. A delivered request with a missing reply does not establish an exchange. Missing directed evidence is unreachable. Reference health, availability, labels and delivery facts are read-only; these exercises ask you to repair configuration using that evidence, not edit a firewall or send packets.

concepts.title: Policy and preservation are outcomes too
concepts.text: A device can synchronize through a source that the assignment does not allow. Meet every required node’s source policy, then preserve any specifically protected downstream and peer associations. A future error invalidates current completion. Reset only this assignment starts its supplied configuration again; the separate example and other saved activities have independent state.

concepts.title: Limits of these observations
concepts.text: This is a small supplied IPv4 dependency graph with one upstream per device. It does not implement clock convergence, offsets, delay, jitter, polling, reach registers, multiple-source selection, authentication, DNS, IPv6, ntp master or NTP packets. No host command, socket, clock adjustment or daemon is used. Read-only statuses describe this model only.

lesson.description: A separate Aspen-relay example uses different addresses, a different existing downstream client and a protected peer. Select and run each command explicitly; inserting only prepares a draft. The assignment has separate state.

worked.explanation: Read the initial unconfigured relay; this does not change it.

The separate client was already configured to this relay; inspect the complete current chain.

lesson.try_change: After the example passes, remove the relay’s configured source. Observe that its unchanged downstream client also becomes unsynchronized. Restore exactly the removed source and check both nodes again.

experiment.explanation: Remove only the example relay source; this intentionally breaks its downstream dependency.

repair.explanation: Restore the removed example source and verify both current nodes.

scenarios.title: Recover a configured dependency cycle
scenarios.summary: Atlas-relay and Birch-relay currently depend on each other, while Floor-client points to an unknown address. Preserve Protected-peer. You may break the cycle at either relay or configure both to references.

Preserve Protected-peer’s supplied association. Do not change supplied delivery facts; request success alone is insufficient.

Bypassing the relays or rewriting downstream settings does not satisfy this handover.
